links.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified online patient education materials from AHA, ACS and ASA websites
links.outcome: Readability (grade level and other indices) of patient education materials, with accuracy and PEMAT-U understandability as balancing measures
links.effect: Mean grade level fell from 10.1 (original) to 7.6 with ChatGPT, 6.6 with Gemini and 5.6 with Claude (all P<.001). Original website means were 10.7 (AHA), 10.0 (ACS) and 9.6 (ASA). Word counts fell from a mean range of 410.9-953.9 to 201.9-248.1. Baseline PEMAT-U understandability was preserved.
links.tradeoff: 3.3% of Gemini and Claude simplified PEMs were inaccurate (none for ChatGPT). Model performance varied, and the authors say human review of LLM output is needed. Word counts were substantially reduced.
links.quote: After optimization by the LLMs, readability scores significantly improved across all 3 websites when compared with the original text.

design_hint: reading-level simplification prompts for patient materials
